title: webpage-note
summary: A small opt-in JavaScript widget that lets website owners and reviewers attach notes to page elements and turn them into prefilled GitHub issues for follow-up.

narrative.problem: Website owners and reviewers lack a common way to leave feedback tied to the exact element they mean: a feedback issue form can ask for a URL and a screenshot, but it cannot attach a comment to an individual part of the page.
narrative.decision: Ships as one dependency-free script, off unless configured, that keeps notes locally and opens a prefilled GitHub issue with the comment, page URL, CSS selector and captured text, with no GitHub token and no automatic submission.
narrative.tradeoff: Reviewers must review and submit each issue themselves and need permission to create issues; submitted issues are not synced back onto the page, and selectors can go stale when the page structure changes.
narrative.limitation: There is no test runner or build tooling, so validation is a syntax check plus manual browser testing; notes inside iframes or shadow DOM are not supported, and saves from multiple tabs overwrite each other.

images.alt: Document excerpt card titled Reviewing and publishing, quoting the README: right-click an element to write a comment, optionally selecting text first to capture it.
images.caption: The core interaction: a note is pinned to the element or text a reviewer right-clicks.
